shortDescription: AI-powered application error monitoring that automatically groups similar errors, identifies root causes, assigns issues to the right developer, and surfaces the most impactful errors to fix first.
summary:
Sentry is the most widely used application error and performance monitoring platform, processing billions of errors from millions of applications globally. AI features elevate Sentry from a raw error log to an intelligent triage and prioritisation system.

Sentry AI auto-groups similar errors into coherent issues rather than flooding developers with thousands of individual error events — when the same bug triggers in a million user sessions, Sentry groups them as one issue with occurrence count rather than a million separate alerts.

Autofix, Sentry's generative AI feature, analyses an error trace, the relevant code, and the repository context to suggest a specific code fix. Rather than developers manually following a stack trace through source code to identify the root cause, Autofix proposes the change most likely to resolve the issue — reducing mean time to fix for common error patterns.

AI-powered issue prioritisation scores each error by user impact, frequency, and regression status — surfacing which errors are most worth fixing first rather than presenting an undifferentiated list of all errors. For teams triaging hundreds of issues, priority scoring focuses developer attention where it matters most.

Seer, Sentry's AI copilot for debugging, allows developers to ask questions about issues ('why is this error occurring in the checkout service?') and receive AI-generated explanations from the error data, traces, and code context.

Labeling functions are programmatic rules, heuristics, and pattern matchers that vote on labels for each data point — encoding domain expert knowledge as code that scales to millions of examples. Multiple imperfect functions are combined through a label model that learns function accuracy.

Data programming enables subject matter experts to contribute labeling knowledge through programmatic functions rather than annotation tools — domain expertise encoded as code scales without proportional annotation workforce cost.

Snorkel's approach is particularly valuable in regulated industries where training data for sensitive models cannot be handled by general annotation workforce providers.

summary:
Signifyd is a commerce fraud protection platform that combines ML fraud detection with a financial guarantee — when Signifyd approves an order and the order later turns out to be fraudulent, Signifyd reimburses the merchant for the chargeback. This guaranteed fraud protection model aligns Signifyd's incentives with merchants: Signifyd absorbs the cost of fraud on approved orders.

The Signifyd Commerce Network is the ML foundation — a consortium of merchant transaction data from thousands of global retailers providing the behavioural patterns needed to distinguish legitimate customers from fraudsters at order approval speed. Network effects make the model more accurate as more merchants share anonymised signals.

ML order decisioning analyses hundreds of signals per order — device fingerprinting, IP geolocation, email and payment history, shipping behaviour, and order characteristics — producing a real-time fraud score and approval decision in milliseconds. Chargeback rates for Signifyd-approved orders are dramatically lower than industry averages.

Account takeover protection monitors login and account activity for behaviour indicating compromised credentials — detecting account takeover attempts before fraudulent orders are placed.

Abuse prevention extends beyond fraud to policy abuse — detecting coupon stacking, return fraud, and loyalty programme abuse from customers who exploit promotions rather than commit traditional payment fraud.

With customers including Samsung, Puma, and Holt Renfrew, Signifyd validates for enterprise commerce fraud at global retailer scale.

Consumer Data Platform integrations connect LiveRamp to CRMs, data warehouses, and marketing platforms — making identity-resolved data available across the marketing technology stack.

With customers including major US retailers, media companies, and financial services firms, LiveRamp is the advertising data infrastructure standard.
